blocks.raw: # Configure Journey
blocks.text: Configure Journey

blocks.raw: This section provides you with information on how to configure a journey.
blocks.text: This section provides you with information on how to configure a journey.

blocks.raw: To configure a journey perform the following steps:
blocks.text: To configure a journey perform the following steps:

blocks.raw: # Step 1: <Anchor target="_blank" href="https://docs.capillarytech.com/docs/configure-journey#/configuring-the-entry-trigger">Configure the entry trigger</Anchor>
blocks.text: Step 1: Configure the entry trigger

blocks.raw: Define how and when a customer enters the Journey. You can define an entry trigger based on a **user event** or **audience list**. For example, when a customer signs up, makes a purchase, or meets a specific condition, or defines an [audience group](https://docs.capillarytech.com/docs/create-audience-group#/) to include specific customers in the journey.

blocks.raw: # Step 2: <Anchor target="_blank" href="https://docs.capillarytech.com/docs/configure-journey#/adding-the-building-blocks">Add the building blocks</Anchor>
blocks.text: Step 2: Add the building blocks

blocks.raw: This is where you design the core path of your Journey. Add the sequence of actions and communications, such as sending an email,  updating customer data, or issuing incentives such as points that will guide the customer toward the desired outcome.

blocks.text: Step 4: Define the schedule for the Journey

blocks.raw: Specify when and how often the journey runs. You can choose to start it immediately, at a specific time, or on a recurring schedule.
blocks.text: Specify when and how often the journey runs. You can choose to start it immediately, at a specific time, or on a recurring schedule.

blocks.raw: The conversion goal lets you define a specific goal and strategy for a journey. This helps track and measure the journey’s performance against the defined goal.
blocks.text: The conversion goal lets you define a specific goal and strategy for a journey. This helps track and measure the journey’s performance against the defined goal.

blocks.raw: # Step 6: <Anchor target="_blank" href="https://docs.capillarytech.com/docs/configure-journey#/configuring-exit-trigger-optional">Configure the exit trigger</Anchor>

blocks.raw: Define the conditions that will remove a customer from the journey. This is crucial for ensuring customers exit once they have completed the desired action (like making a purchase) or reached the end of the path, preventing them from receiving unnecessary communications.

blocks.raw: # Configuring the entry trigger
blocks.text: Configuring the entry trigger

blocks.raw: To configure an entry trigger, perform the following steps:
blocks.text: To configure an entry trigger, perform the following steps:

blocks.raw:
1. On the **Journey Canvas** page, select **Entry Trigger** to define how customers will enter the journey.

2. Select the type of entry trigger - **User Event** or **Audience List**. Note

3. For **User Event:** From the **Who have performed the event** drop-down, select the desired event type - <Anchor target="_blank" href="https://docs.capillarytech.com/docs/configure-events-and-conditions#/adding-transactional-events">**Transactional Event**</Anchor> or <Anchor target="_blank" href="https://docs.capillarytech.com/docs/configure-events-and-conditions#/adding-behavioral-events">**Behavioral Event**</Anchor>.

   **Notes**: Attribute-based entry trigger configuration is not enabled by default. To use this capability, raise a Jira ticket to the Product Support team to enable it for your organization.

   When using the Exact match type in Entry Trigger conditions, the configured value must exactly match the corresponding event attribute value, including any leading or trailing spaces. If either the configured value or the event attribute contains unintended spaces, the condition will not match, and the customer will not enter the Journey.

blocks.raw: # Scheduling the journey
blocks.text: Scheduling the journey

blocks.raw:
1. Select the **Journey controls** block to begin configuring the journey schedule. In the schedule tab of the journey controls modal, configure the start and end dates for the journey. 2. In the **Starts** section, there are two options. 1. **Immediately after approval**: Start the journey as soon as it is approved by an administrator. 2. **On a specific date**: Start the journey on a specific date. Select the date from the calendar box.
**Note**: A 3-hour buffer applies when selecting same day execution. For example, if you select today's date and approve the journey at 10:00 AM, the journey will not start until approximately 1:00 PM. Plan your start time accordingly to avoid unexpected delays. 3. In the **Ends** section, there are two options 1. **Never**: Run a journey without an expiration date. 2. **On a specific date**: End the journey on a specific date. Select the date from the calendar box.

blocks.raw: # Configuring the conversion goal (optional):
blocks.text: Configuring the conversion goal (optional):

blocks.raw: The journey conversion goal lets you define a specific goal and strategy for a journey. This helps track and measure the journey’s performance against the defined goal. Each journey supports one conversion goal.
blocks.text: The journey conversion goal lets you define a specific goal and strategy for a journey. This helps track and measure the journey’s performance against the defined goal. Each journey supports one conversion goal.

blocks.raw: ## **Use case:**
blocks.text: Use case:

blocks.raw: #### **Requirement:**
blocks.text: Requirement:

blocks.raw: A retail brand wants to track how many customers complete their online purchase within 3 days of receiving an abandoned cart reminder email.
blocks.text: A retail brand wants to track how many customers complete their online purchase within 3 days of receiving an abandoned cart reminder email.

blocks.raw: #### **Solution:**

blocks.raw:
* Conversion Event: Bill Lineitems
* Condition: `include` whose `Order Channel` is `Online`
* Eligible Period: 3 Days
* Tracking Starts: Delivered'

1. On the canvas, select the **Journey Controls** block and open the **Conversion goal** settings. 2. From the dropdown menu, select the **conversion event** you want to track, for example, **Bill Lineitems** 3. Define the conversion criteria by selecting **+Add conditions**. Use the **AND** (**+Add condition**) and **OR** (**+Add condition group**) operators to build your logic based on the event's attributes. 4. Under **Eligible period for conversion**, define the lookback window, for example, five days, and select when tracking should begin.
The following table details the available options to define when tracking begins:

blocks.raw: # Configuring exit trigger (Optional)
blocks.text: Configuring exit trigger (Optional)

blocks.raw: An exit trigger is to remove a customer from a journey if they satisfy a given condition. Brands can configure transactional and behavioral events that can cause a customer to exit a journey. This ensures that customers do not get spam/out-of-context engagements.
blocks.text: An exit trigger is to remove a customer from a journey if they satisfy a given condition. Brands can configure transactional and behavioral events that can cause a customer to exit a journey. This ensures that customers do not get spam/out-of-context engagements.

blocks.raw: ## Use Cases
blocks.text: Use Cases

blocks.raw:
* A brand wants to target customers who have purchased shoes from them and want to motivate them to buy clothes as well. If a customer has already purchased from the clothes category, they should not receive promotional messages to buy clothes which can be configured in the exit trigger.
* Brands want to motivate users by asking them to upgrade to members. Customers who purchased the membership should be exited from the membership promotional journey

If a customer has already purchased from the clothes category, they should not receive promotional messages to buy clothes which can be configured in the exit trigger.Brands want to motivate users by asking them to upgrade to members. Customers who purchased the membership should be exited from the membership promotional journey

blocks.raw: ## Removing an exit trigger
blocks.text: Removing an exit trigger

blocks.raw: This allows you to remove an existing exit condition from a journey, giving you the flexibility to control when customers should no longer exit based on that trigger. You can remove the exit trigger when the journey is in **Draft** or **Live** state, as long as an exit trigger is already configured.
blocks.text: This allows you to remove an existing exit condition from a journey, giving you the flexibility to control when customers should no longer exit based on that trigger. You can remove the exit trigger when the journey is in Draft or Live state, as long as an exit trigger is already configured.

blocks.raw: To remove an exit trigger perform the following steps
blocks.text: To remove an exit trigger perform the following steps

blocks.raw:
1. On the journey listing page navigate to the journey that has exit trigger configured.
2. Select the journey and on the journey canvas navigate to **Journey controls**.
3. Select the edit icon to open the configuration modal, then select **Exit Trigger**.
4. Navigate to the three dots and select **Remove exit trigger**.
5. A confirmation modal appears. Select **Yes, remove** to proceed.

blocks.text: The following conditions must be satisfied for a customer to enter or re-enter the journey. You can configure the settings as follows:

blocks.raw:
1. **Frequency of a customer entering the journey**- Set how many times a customer is allowed to enter the journey. 2. **Customer can be in this journey simultaneously**- Allow a customer to be part of the journey more than once at the same time if the customer meets the entry conditions again.

**Note**: This setting is applicable only for journeys with event-based entry triggers. It is not supported for audience-based journeys. For event-based journeys, choosing "More than once" or "Specific number of times" also requires your account to be set up to support it. If you select one of these and the journey fails validation at Send for Approval, raise a Jira ticket to the Product Support Team to check your account configuration.

blocks.raw: ### Scenario 1 - Ticket Confirmation Reminder

blocks.raw: ## Test and control ratio for a journey
blocks.text: Test and control ratio for a journey

blocks.raw: The test and control ratio lets you divide the users entering a journey into two groups: a **test group** that receives all the communications and incentives configured in the journey, and a **control group** that moves through the journey without receiving any communications or incentives. By comparing the behavior of both groups, you can measure the true impact of your journey on customer actions such as purchases, visits, or conversions.
blocks.text: The test and control ratio lets you divide the users entering a journey into two groups: a test group that receives all the communications and incentives configured in the journey, and a control group that moves through the journey without receiving any communications or incentives. By comparing the behavior of both groups, you can measure the true impact of your journey on customer actions such as purchases, visits, or conversions.

blocks.raw: **Note:** The test and control configuration is set once when you create a journey and cannot be changed after the journey goes live.
blocks.text: Note: The test and control configuration is set once when you create a journey and cannot be changed after the journey goes live.

blocks.raw: ### How the test and control work
blocks.text: How the test and control work

blocks.raw: You can enable the test and control ratio for a journey to split users entering the journey into two groups based on the percentage you set.
blocks.text: You can enable the test and control ratio for a journey to split users entering the journey into two groups based on the percentage you set.

blocks.raw:
| Group       | What happens                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| ----------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Test**    | Users receive all communications and incentives configured in the journey                                                                                                                                 |
| **Control** | Users move through all the blocks in the journey, but all engagement actions are skipped. No messages are sent, and no incentives are issued. Users are still tracked for events and appear in analytics. |

rows: Users receive all communications and incentives configured in the journey

Users move through all the blocks in the journey, but all engagement actions are skipped. No messages are sent, and no incentives are issued. Users are still tracked for events and appear in analytics.

blocks.text: What the control group experiences

blocks.raw: Control group users are not aware they're in the control group. They continue to interact with the brand as usual, without receiving any communications or incentives from this journey.
blocks.text: Control group users are not aware they're in the control group. They continue to interact with the brand as usual, without receiving any communications or incentives from this journey.

blocks.raw:
| Journey action                                         | Test group         | Control group                     |
| ------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------ | --------------------------------- |
| SMS, email, push, WhatsApp, and other channel messages | Sent normally      | Skipped, not sent                 |
| Incentives (points, rewards)                           | Issued normally    | Skipped, not issued               |
| Wait, decision split, join, and jump blocks            | Processed normally | Processed normally                |
| Event tracking                                         | Tracked            | Tracked                           |
| Analytics                                              | Logged normally    | Logged as skipped (control group) |

blocks.raw: ### Effective test percentage
blocks.text: Effective test percentage

blocks.raw: The actual percentage of users who receive communications depends on two values: the journey test ratio you set, and your organization's global test percentage. The global test percentage is configured at the org level and may vary.
blocks.text: The actual percentage of users who receive communications depends on two values: the journey test ratio you set, and your organization's global test percentage. The global test percentage is configured at the org level and may vary.

blocks.raw: **Formula:**
blocks.text: Formula:

blocks.raw:
```
Journey test % = (Journey test ratio × Global test %) ÷ 100
```

code.code: Journey test % = (Journey test ratio × Global test %) ÷ 100

blocks.raw: **Example:** If your org's global test percentage is 90% and you set a journey test ratio of 35%, then 31.5% of users entering the journey receive communications.

blocks.raw: The current global test percentage for your org is shown directly in the Journey settings panel.

blocks.raw: ### Frequently asked questions (FAQs)
blocks.text: Frequently asked questions (FAQs)

blocks.raw: **1. What is the purpose of setting up Journey Alerts?** Journey Alerts are automated email notifications designed to keep you informed about critical events in your marketing journeys. They enable you to proactively monitor campaigns for approval requests, execution failures, or upcoming end dates, allowing you to take timely action and ensure your campaigns run smoothly.
blocks.text: 1. What is the purpose of setting up Journey Alerts? Journey Alerts are automated email notifications designed to keep you informed about critical events in your marketing journeys. They enable you to proactively monitor campaigns for approval requests, execution failures, or upcoming end dates, allowing you to take timely action and ensure your campaigns run smoothly.

blocks.raw: **2. I'm trying to add a team member to the notification list, but I'm unable to find them. Why?** The person selection dropdown list shows only people who are configured as a point of contact (POC) for your organization. If you can't find a team member, an administrator must first add them to the [organization POC](https://docs.capillarytech.com/docs/org-management#/organization-point-of-contact-tab) list.
blocks.text: 2. I'm trying to add a team member to the notification list, but I'm unable to find them. Why? The person selection dropdown list shows only people who are configured as a point of contact (POC) for your organization. If you can't find a team member, an administrator must first add them to the organization POC list.

blocks.raw: **3. If I set the expiry alert to seven days in advance, will I get a notification every day for those seven days?** No. The alert is sent only once. You will receive a single notification exactly seven days before the journey is scheduled to expire, providing you with a one-time notification.
blocks.text: 3. If I set the expiry alert to seven days in advance, will I get a notification every day for those seven days? No. The alert is sent only once. You will receive a single notification exactly seven days before the journey is scheduled to expire, providing you with a one-time notification.

blocks.raw: **4. Can I apply these alert settings to a specific journey only?** No, the current alert settings are global. When you configure a person to get an alert (for example, a status change alert), they will get that alert for all journeys created on the platform. Journey-specific alert settings aren't currently available.
blocks.text: 4. Can I apply these alert settings to a specific journey only? No, the current alert settings are global. When you configure a person to get an alert (for example, a status change alert), they will get that alert for all journeys created on the platform. Journey-specific alert settings aren't currently available.

blocks.raw: **5. How are the alerts delivered?** All Journey Alerts are delivered by email to the people you select in the configuration.
blocks.text: 5. How are the alerts delivered? All Journey Alerts are delivered by email to the people you select in the configuration.

blocks.raw: **6. Is there any retry mechanism if the message fails to send** No, there is no retry mechanism if the message fails to send.
